title: Feedback form template (Microsoft Forms)
subject: English
source: Written for english/y6 lesson 43 (Feedback form template (Microsoft Forms))
intro: Lesson 43: What does a school website need? Evaluating the TGA website with a feedback form. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Audience
Needs
rows: what the school is like, how to join

model.title: Evaluate: can a parent find how to contact the school?

parts.text: Look for Contact in the menu
Judge: easy, quite easy or hard, with a reason

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: For example: Easy: Contact is in the top menu, one click away.

keywords.def: how you move around a website: menus, links, buttons
the main page of a website
judge how good something is, with reasons
a set of questions to collect people's views

questions.q: Write a closed question for the feedback form
questions.a: For example: Was it easy to find the term dates? Yes / No
For example: What one change would improve the homepage?

questions.q: Name one thing parents need from a school website
Core: evaluate the website against four criteria with a reason each, then write a five-question feedback form for parents (three closed, two open) in Microsoft Forms or on paper
questions.a: An evaluation and a five-question form

questions.q: Extend: write a short polite note to parents explaining the purpose of the form
questions.a: For example: Dear parents and carers, Year 6 would be grateful if you could complete this short form to help us improve the school website.

questions.q: Stretch: explain why accessibility matters on a website
questions.a: So everyone, including people with visual or other needs, can use it

questions.q: Which is a useful criterion for judging a website?
options: Important information is easy to find.
questions.a: B) Important information is easy to find.. B links to what users need. A is personal taste; C is not always good.
